newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST - Portugal May yr/yr inflation to slow.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Portugal May yr/yr inflation to slow.

text.p: Seven out of eight analysts polled by Reuters expect Portugal's year-on-year inflation to ease in May from April's 1.8 percent, with one analyst seeing the rate unchanged.
The National Statistics Institute will release the official figure on June 17, officials said.
Analysts' forecasts for the month-on-month rise in the consumer price index (CPI) varied from 0.1 to 0.4 percent against 0.2 percent in April.
An increase of 0.1 percent would give a year-on-year rise of 1.4 or 1.5 percent, while 0.4 percent increase would result in a year-on-year gain of 1.8 percent.
The rolling 12-month average, the government's benchmark rate, would ease to 3.0 percent whether the monthly rate was 0.1 or 0.4 percent, from 3.1 percent in April, analysts said.
The main reason for the expected easing in the year-on-year inflation rate is that the sharp increase in food prices triggered last year by the so-called mad cow disease is slipping out of the index.
In May 1996, the month-on-month rise was 0.3 percent and the year-on-year increase 3.5 percent.
Analysts whose forecasts for May were at the higher end of the range pointed to rises in pork prices and increases in tobacco. On the other side of the scale, however, potato prices have fallen.
